files.purpose: Introduces Hafþi OS, its current limitations, and how to download, build and test it.
files.when: Read before trying the prototype or making your first build.
details: The current image is an x86_64 live preview. It does not install an operating system to a disk.
Niri, Hafþi and Google Chrome describe the planned installed desktop; the live prototype uses Cage and GTK.
The download is a GitHub Actions artifact containing the ISO, checksum and measured size.

files.purpose: Keeps generated build output, VM screenshots and Python bytecode out of version control.
files.when: Git uses it when deciding which untracked files to offer for staging.
details: out/ contains ISO builds and test output. preview/ contains downloaded VM diagnostics.
__pycache__/ and *.pyc are generated by Python.
Ignoring a path does not delete it and does not remove a file that was already committed.

files.purpose: Runs the automated checks, builds the ISO, boots a disposable VM and uploads download artifacts.
files.when: GitHub Actions runs it for pushes to main or a manual workflow dispatch.
details: The runner is Ubuntu; the image is built inside a privileged Arch Linux container because Archiso needs mount operations.
The container installs Archiso, GRUB and Python, then builds from the official baseline profile.
The output is handed back to the runner for the VM test. The VM uses a temporary virtual disk, not a host disk.
hafthiOS-prototype contains the ISO; hafthiOS-preview contains the screenshot, serial log and size report. Artifacts currently expire after 14 days.
A successful build and BIOS VM test do not establish compatibility with every graphics card, wireless device, UEFI firmware or Secure Boot setup.

files.purpose: Builds the bootable live ISO and embeds the offline file guide and source snapshots.
files.when: Run as root on an Arch build host; CI runs it inside its build container.
details: Copies /usr/share/archiso/configs/baseline into a temporary build workspace. It does not edit the system-wide baseline.
Copies live/ into the image root and installs the guide under /usr/share/doc/hafthios/.
The package list contains the live kernel, Cage, Foot, GTK, Python, Mesa, NetworkManager, Polkit and fonts. It does not include the planned installed desktop.
Sets Hafþi OS branding and uses SquashFS with xz compression. Adds executable permissions for the two session programs.
Enables NetworkManager in the live image, then invokes mkarchiso to produce out/*.iso.
Writes a SHA256 checksum and size.txt. A marketed 1 GB USB target means less than 1,000,000,000 bytes.
The temporary build workspace is removed on exit. No selected installation disk is partitioned, formatted or mounted.

Installs Plymouth, applies the quiet boot configuration, and masks the default early quit/wait services. The tty1 getty releases Plymouth with retain-splash just before starting the graphical session.

files.purpose: Checks that every project file has a guide entry, then bundles the guide and an exact copy of each documented source file.
files.when: During ISO creation; it can also be run directly for a local documentation check.
details: The repository file inventory excludes Git internals, generated output, downloaded previews and Python bytecode.
Missing explanations stop the bundle build, so a new project file cannot silently disappear from the guide.
Copies documented source files into sources/ while preserving their relative paths. The reader never executes these snapshots.
Rejects absolute paths and parent-directory traversal in the catalog.
The same documentation directory can be copied into a future installed system; the current prototype has no target installation backend.

files.purpose: Boots the ISO in QEMU, checks that the welcome screen and offline guide open, and saves screenshots and logs.
files.when: After a successful image build in GitHub Actions.
details: Uses software CPU emulation, 2 GB RAM, a virtual graphics device and a disposable 16 GiB sparse disk.
Waits for HAFTHIOS_GUI_READY in the serial log, then saves the welcome screenshot.
Sends F1 through QEMU to open the offline guide and waits for HAFTHIOS_GUIDE_READY.
Captures diagnostics on failure and terminates the VM when the test ends.
This is a BIOS VM smoke test. It is not a destructive installation test or a real-hardware certification.

Detects the ship splash in screenshots before GTK starts, checks that frames change, presses Esc and verifies the ship artwork disappears for details, then verifies the second Esc restores the ship. Also checks the welcome screen and F1 guide as before.

files.purpose: Makes the live image log in automatically on its first virtual console.
files.when: systemd starts getty@tty1 while the live ISO boots.
details: The empty ExecStart= clears the original getty command. The next ExecStart= launches agetty with --autologin root.
%I expands to the instance name, tty1. --noclear keeps the existing console contents.
This setting is for the disposable live image. It must not be copied unchanged into a future installed desktop.
ExecStartPre asks Plymouth to quit while retaining its last frame, releasing graphics before Cage starts. A missing or unavailable Plymouth is nonfatal.

files.purpose: Starts the graphical session when the live root account logs in on tty1.
files.when: Bash reads it as the live login shell starts.
details: The tty check limits automatic graphical startup to /dev/tty1.
Other consoles remain available for troubleshooting.
If the graphical session exits, the login shell remains. No target disk installation is triggered.

files.purpose: Sets up the live graphical environment and launches the welcome application inside Cage.
files.when: Called by the live login profile on tty1.
details: Creates the live root runtime directory with mode 700.
GDK_BACKEND=wayland makes GTK use Wayland. GTK_THEME selects the dark theme.
WLR_RENDERER=pixman and GSK_RENDERER=cairo select software rendering for this initial prototype.
If a serial device is present, session output goes there for VM diagnostics.
dbus-run-session supplies a private session bus; Cage is the small Wayland compositor hosting the welcome window. This is not the planned Niri desktop.

files.purpose: Implements the graphical welcome screen, disk preview, proposed-system summary, and offline guide reader.
files.when: Cage launches it on live boot. Run hafthios-welcome --guide to open the guide directly.
details: Install Hafþi OS opens a preview flow. It does not install, erase, partition or mount a selected disk.
read_disks uses the read-only lsblk JSON query. It lists writable whole disks and excludes partitions, loop devices and read-only devices.
The review screen lists the selected disk and the planned Arch/Niri/Hafþi/Chrome desktop.
Network settings launches nmtui in Foot for the live session. Restart calls systemctl reboot.
The guide is read from /usr/share/doc/hafthios/. A search field filters file names and explanations; each article can show its bundled source snapshot.
F1 opens the guide. Serial markers are used by the VM test to verify that the UI and guide loaded.
The guide source viewer recognises binary assets and displays an explanation instead of attempting to show image bytes as UTF-8 text.

files.purpose: Tests the read-only disk discovery helpers without needing a GTK display.
files.when: Run with python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v.
details: Checks exclusion of partitions, loop devices, optical media and read-only disks.
Mocks lsblk to check disk size formatting and that only the intended read-only query is executed.
Checks the empty-disk case. These tests do not validate physical hardware or perform installation.

files.purpose: Tests catalog coverage, source snapshot packaging and rejection of unsafe catalog paths.
files.when: As part of the normal Python tests before ISO creation.
details: Checks that every project file is documented and each connection points to a known file.
Builds a temporary guide bundle and compares its source snapshots to the repository files.
Tests that a catalog path cannot escape the bundle directory.

files.purpose: Explains how to use the file guide and the scope of the local documentation.
files.when: Read on GitHub or through the bundled source viewer.
details: The guide documents the project-owned files, not every file provided by Arch packages.
The local bundle includes the guide and source snapshots matching that ISO build.
The live prototype is ephemeral. A future installer must copy the documentation bundle to the target system.

files.purpose: Stores one English article for every project-owned file, including this catalog itself.
files.when: The bundler validates it; the GTK guide reader displays it locally.
details: Each article records path, purpose, when it runs, connected files and detailed behavior.
Keep entries consistent with the implementation when changing code. Catalog coverage checks cannot verify the truth of prose automatically.
The catalog is data only. The reader displays its text and does not execute commands from articles.

files.purpose: Brands and quiets the BIOS, UEFI and loopback boot entries.
files.when: While assembling the Archiso profile before mkarchiso runs.
details: Adds quiet splash parameters, enables status collection behind the splash, and prevents deferred framebuffer-console takeover from leaving a stale ship frame in the details view. Retains the official live-medium discovery and loopback arguments. Hides the short UEFI menu, shortens the BIOS menu, and brands entries as Hafthi OS.
Fails if the expected boot entries are absent rather than silently producing an image without the splash. Running it twice does not duplicate parameters.

files.purpose: Checks that quiet boot preserves the arguments needed to find the live ISO.
files.when: During local validation and the CI check step.
details: Uses representative BIOS, UEFI and loopback entries. Verifies discovery arguments survive, quiet parameters appear once, and missing baseline entries fail clearly.

files.purpose: Starts graphics and Plymouth in the live image initramfs.
files.when: Before the main live filesystem is mounted.
details: Keeps the official Archiso discovery hooks and adds kms, keyboard and plymouth after udev. Explicitly loads the PS/2 and USB keyboard drivers before starting Plymouth. The kms hook includes graphics drivers and the keyboard hook makes Esc available before the live filesystem is mounted; Plymouth draws the ship while the live system starts.

files.purpose: Selects the Hafþi OS splash without a display delay.
files.when: When Plymouth starts in the initramfs and during live boot.
details: Theme=hafthios selects the project theme. ShowDelay=0 shows it as soon as the graphics device becomes available.

files.purpose: Registers the ship splash with the Plymouth script renderer.
files.when: When Plymouth loads the selected theme.
details: Points to the script and its artwork directory using paths available in the live image and initramfs.

files.purpose: Animates the supplied ship artwork on a dark boot screen.
files.when: From early live boot until the graphical session takes over.
details: Scales the image proportionally to fit the screen. A refresh callback moves it gently sideways and vertically, suggesting a quiet voyage. The original artwork stays intact.
Shows an Esc hint. Plymouth itself handles Esc to switch between the graphical theme and boot details; this script does not intercept or discard logs.

files.purpose: Contains the user-supplied white Viking ship artwork on a dark background.
files.when: Loaded by the Plymouth theme during startup.
details: A PNG format conversion of the supplied JPEG, preserving its decoded pixels and proportions. This is a binary image, not a text source file.
